text: Add some color coding to chat running state
Now the RowText and status values, plus theme colours.
Colours are in place; now type-checking the app.

I added colours for a run's state, but I haven't type-checked it or looked at it in Firefox. This checkout has no installed packages, so neither check could run here. Please look at the Sessions tab once it lands on the main line.

**The Sessions list:** in each row's grey line, the state word is now coloured:
- **running**: green and bold.
- **queued**: amber.
- **failed**: red and bold.
- **finished** and **stopped**: stay grey.

**The header of an open chat:** the small dot uses the same colours. It also turns amber while a stop is going through, and gets a red ring when the run failed.

The colour choice is one shared helper, `runColour`, in `apps/app/src/ui/theme.ts`, so the list and the chat header always match. The list change is in `apps/app/src/app/(tabs)/chat/index.tsx` and the dot is in `apps/app/src/ui/Conversation.tsx`. I also changed the row's grey line (`RowText` in `apps/app/src/ui/parts.tsx`) so it can hold coloured text, not just plain text.
Refreshed the page, still don't see colors
The change is on the main line. The page you load must come from a build that doesn't have it yet. I'll check how the app gets rebuilt; an earlier chat traced the same thing for the tab bar fix.
The served app was built while the change was landing. It has the new colour helper but still the old Sessions list and chat header, so it needs a rebuild. Checking how builds are triggered.

The colours aren't showing because the app you load is built from files that don't contain them, even though the change itself is on the main line (`29c2f4b`).

**Why:** the app is rebuilt from the files in `C:\Projects\momentum` as they are on disk, not from the main line. That folder has uncommitted edits that add file attachments to chat. They touch the same two files I changed: the Sessions list (`chat/index.tsx`) and the chat header (`Conversation.tsx`). Those edited versions don't have my colouring, so the build has the new colour helper but the old list and header. You still see no colours.

**The risk:** if the attachment edits are committed as they are, they will undo the colouring on the main line too.

I'm not allowed to change that folder from this chat, so I left it alone. Once the attachment work is committed, send me a message here. I'll check whether the colours survived and add them back if they didn't.
I don't give a shit. I want all the changes I request to be fucking built and deployed
I'll split the export into its own script that builds from the main line in a scratch folder, and have the dev runner watch the main line instead of the working files.
Now the dev runner: it polls the main line's app and contract trees and exports when either changes.
Now a test export from this checkout, borrowing the workspace's installed packages through a link and writing to a temporary folder.
The export works from the main line. Checking the colouring is in the bundle, and getting rid of that shell warning.
Both test exports passed. Cleaning up the test links and output, then checking whether any doc describes the old build.
Tested end to end. Now updating the README line that describes the old behaviour.

I changed the build so the app you load always comes from the main line, but the new version only takes over once the development server restarts. Until then you still won't see the colours.

**Cause:** the app was rebuilt from the files in `C:\Projects\momentum` as they sit on disk. That folder holds a large set of uncommitted edits (attachments, back end, tests), and those hid what had landed. It's also why the tab bar fix seemed late earlier today.

**Change:**
- A new script, `scripts/export-web.mjs`, takes the app and the shared types package as committed on the main line and builds the app from that copy. Uncommitted edits never reach what you see.
- The dev server (`scripts/dev.mjs`) now checks the main line every 2 seconds and rebuilds whenever a commit changes the app.
- I updated the README to match.

**Tested:** I ran the new build twice from this checkout and both runs succeeded. The result contains the run-state colours in both the list and the chat header. I haven't opened it in Firefox.

**What you need to do:** restart the server once after this lands: `schtasks /End /TN Momentum` then `schtasks /Run /TN Momentum`, or log off and on. The old process doesn't reload its own code, and I can't restart it from here because this chat runs inside it. After that restart, every change you request is rebuilt as soon as it lands.

**Caveat:** an uncommitted edit in that folder won't show in the app until it's committed.
You dense fucker. What i need to do??? Finish the fucking task
Doing it now. I'll put the colours on the live app straight away, then schedule the server restart myself for once this lands.
The colours are live now. Next, the one-time restart so every future change is built from the main line too.

You don't need to do anything. The colours are live now: refresh the page.

- **Now:** I rebuilt the app from the main line straight into what the server shows, at 17:40. The new build contains the colours for running, queued and failed, in the list and in the chat header.
- **From now on:** the server now builds only from committed code, so uncommitted edits in `C:\Projects\momentum` can't hide your changes. It needs one restart to start using that, and I've set that up to happen automatically. About a minute after this chat's changes land, it restarts the server itself. Within roughly 15 seconds the app comes back, building from the main line.
- **During the restart:** the app is offline for those 15 seconds or so, and any automation that happens to be running at that moment is stopped. If the restart doesn't happen, the log at `%TEMP%\momentum-restart.log` will say so.

I also updated the knowledge base to describe the new build: [Web export from main](Architecture/Workflow/web-export-from-main) is new, and the [Back-end](Architecture/Service/backend) entry now matches.
